If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending up, increase forecast by 1.0–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% for the next 7 days to reflect volatility.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, cap forecast at 10% below recent low for late horizon to avoid downward traps.  
If sentiment is positive but price is declining, apply a 1.5–2.0% upward correction for mid horizon to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.
